{LEADING_LABEL}

Optional

Your leadership journey

A way to grow as a leader at your own pace, from a first interest in leading to setting direction for others.

There is no nomination, no group to join and no deadline. You choose where to start and how fast to go. {LEADING_PRIVACY_SENTENCE} How this works.

How one round works

Each round is small: one lesson, a few lines of reflection, one thing tried in your real work, and a note on what happened. Then you go around again.

    {JOURNEY_STEPS.map(step =>
  1. {step.title}. {step.body} {step.link}.
    2. )}

Most of what makes someone a better leader comes from trying things in real work. Some comes from other people: a colleague, a mentor, a team. A small part comes from lessons. So the lessons here are short, and each one leads to something to try.

Find a starting point

Answer two or three questions about your work, or simply choose from the list below.

    {LEADING_PATHS.map(path =>
  • {path.title} {PATH_JOURNEY[path.slug] ? {PATH_JOURNEY[path.slug].question} : {path.description}} Open this path
    • )}

A steady rhythm

A week that fits inside real work looks something like this. Take less when the week is full.

    {WEEKLY_RHYTHM.map(item =>
  • {item.what}: {item.time}
    • )}
One way to pace a path over six weeks
    {SIX_WEEKS.map(week =>
  1. Week {week.week}. Learn: {week.learn}. Reflect: {week.reflect}. Apply: {week.apply}.
    2. )}

This is one example. Any path can be taken faster, slower or in a different order.

Looking back

Reflection is what turns a lesson into a change. A few lines are enough, and three questions carry most of it: what happened, why it matters, and what you will do next. Open your reflection notebook.

    {REFLECTION_PROMPTS.map(prompt =>
  • {prompt.kind}. {prompt.when} {prompt.questions.join(" ")}
    • )}

When you set a date to look back, the notebook shows it to you the next time you open it. Nothing is sent as a reminder.

Learning with others, if you want to

None of this is required. A conversation with someone you trust can deepen what you notice.

    {LEARNING_WITH_OTHERS.map(place =>
  • {place.title}{place.body}
    • )}

Free courses elsewhere

For anyone who wants more. These belong to other organizations, open on their sites, and may ask you to create an account there. They do not count toward required training unless your manager, director or agency leadership approves an exception.

    {LEARNING_ELSEWHERE.map(course =>
  • {course.title}, {course.provider}. {course.body}
    • )}

At the end of a path

Four questions to ask yourself:

    {END_OF_PATH_QUESTIONS.map(question =>
  • {question}
    • )}

There is nothing to submit, and nothing here is counted or rated. If you want something to bring to a development conversation, download your action plans and reflections from My work. What you share, and with whom, is your choice.

import type { Metadata } from "next"; import Link from "@/components/app-link"; import { LEADING_LABEL, LEADING_PRIVACY_SENTENCE, REQUIRED_COURSE_LABEL, TRIBAL_REFERRAL_HREF } from "@/lib/content/collections"; import { TRAINING_CREDIT_NOTICE } from "@/lib/program/learning-credit"; import base from "@/app/learn/collaboration/collaboration.module.css"; import styles from "@/components/collections.module.css"; export const metadata: Metadata = { title: `How this works | ${LEADING_LABEL}`, description: "What is and is not recorded in the leadership space, and where your progress and questions go.", }; export default function LeadingHowThisWorksPage() { return

{LEADING_LABEL}

{LEADING_LABEL}

How this works

What is recorded, what is not, and what this space does not do.

There is no team view

{LEADING_PRIVACY_SENTENCE}

  • There is no sign-in for this space. All of it is public, and staff can read every page.
  • There is no team view, no assignments and no scores.
  • A supervisor cannot see who opened a course, how far they got or what they answered. Neither can you.

What stays in your browser

  • Your progress stays in your browser. That includes your place on a suggested path, your lesson progress and your practice answers.
  • Nothing is sent to a supervisor or employer.
  • Anyone using the same computer and browser could see it. You can clear it at any time.

What happens to a question in Ask

  • Questions typed into Ask go to outside services so that it can answer.
  • The current service does not intentionally save a question-and-answer copy in the owner workspace. Operational activity may be recorded, and earlier versions may have retained separate records. Supervisors do not receive your browser conversation from Ask.
  • Please do not type anyone's name, case, health or personnel details. Ask general questions.

What this does not replace

  • This app does not replace training the state requires. It does not count as the training Minn. Stat. 43A.21 requires of supervisors and managers. The state's own training does that.
  • It is general information, not legal advice. For a real situation, ask Human Resources, labor relations or your ADA coordinator.
  • It does not make or record any personnel, accommodation or complaint decision.

The one exception to voluntary use

{TRAINING_CREDIT_NOTICE}

The Equity Analysis Toolkit is required of all staff of the Minnesota Department of Human Services, regardless of status, so it is marked “{REQUIRED_COURSE_LABEL}” wherever it is listed here. This app does not assign it or report on who has taken it. Open the Equity Analysis Toolkit course.

Using the learning

Use these courses as guidance for your work, alongside current policy and the people and offices responsible for a decision.

Tribal and Native American learning

This space does not offer Tribal curriculum. One DSD refers Native American and Tribal-specific learning, questions and engagement to ADSA and the responsible Tribal liaison. Native American and Tribal-specific guidance.

Keep exploring

What are you deciding?How participation and privacy work across the program
